teaser: A 7 who is also an INFJ is a seeker with a second job: the 7 goes looking for what is true, and the INFJ wants to know what that truth is for, and for whom. Neither system says this alone. The number on its own would be content in a quiet room with a good question. The letters on their own would be content helping someone across the street. Together they make a person who studies in private and then comes back out, unasked, carrying something meant for somebody else.
number:
The 7 is the seeker's number, the one that bridges what can be measured and what can only be sensed, and it asks for long stretches of solitude to do that work. Reached through 16, the old Tower, it carries a further note: the structures this number builds in its head are tested, sometimes knocked down, and rebuilt more honestly than before.

In an INFJ the seeking turns inward first. Introverted intuition does the 7's patient looking almost without effort; the pattern arrives before the argument for it. What the 7 adds is the demand that the pattern hold up under scrutiny. This pairing does not settle for a hunch, however sure the hunch feels. In love the 7 is slow to be known, and the INFJ is slower still to admit how much it already knows about the other person. A partner who respects the quiet tends to find, in time, that the quiet was full of attention. At work the pairing does well wherever careful study ends in something useful to people: research that someone reads, a diagnosis someone acts on.
type:
The INFJ leads with a far-sighted intuition and steers by a warm attention to the people in the room. The letters describe someone who sees where things are heading and wants others to arrive there intact. Under a 7 that warmth acquires a filter. The type's usual readiness to take up a cause slows down; this INFJ wants to understand the cause completely before lending it a name.

The habit of reading people stays, but it becomes quieter and more exact. Where another INFJ might rush to reassure, this one watches a little longer, asks one more question, and offers the reassurance only when it is true. The type's known risk is burning out on other people's needs. The 7 gives it a built-in remedy, an appetite for retreat that the INFJ alone might feel guilty about. Here the withdrawal reads less like escape and more like the place the next insight is assembled. Friends sometimes mistake the silence for distance. It is usually closer to concentration, with them somewhere inside it.
agree:
Both systems point at the same quality: depth that does not show its working. The 7 is the number of the researcher and the philosopher; the INFJ is the type that sees patterns others miss. Laid over each other they describe a mind that is always a few steps under the surface of a conversation, noticing what is not being said and why.

In ordinary life this looks like the colleague who stays quiet in the meeting and then, the next morning, sends the one message that changes the plan. It looks like the friend who remembers the offhand remark from a year ago and turns out to have been thinking about it since. It looks like a bookshelf with more margin notes than spine creases. Both systems agree that this person does their best thinking alone and their best giving with one or two people at a time, never a crowd. And both agree that the private work is real work, even when nobody else can see it from outside.
pull:
The tension is between the 7's need to doubt and the INFJ's need to help. The number wants every claim tested, its own most of all; the letters want to act on what they see, because someone is waiting. A 7 can sit with an open question for years and call it honesty. An INFJ finds that same open question unbearable when a person they care about is on the other end of it.

The result is a familiar loop. The INFJ half sees what a friend needs and is ready to say so. The 7 half asks how it could possibly be sure, and the moment passes. Later the INFJ half regrets the silence, and the 7 half files the regret as one more thing to examine. Neither half is wrong. The 16 adds its own edge: this pairing tends to learn most when a long-held certainty gives way, and those moments rarely feel like learning while they are happening. The pull does not resolve. It is part of how this pairing thinks.
closing: That is the reading for a 7 and an INFJ. Take what is useful, leave the rest, and come back to it later to see which parts have moved.
